A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching research questions, sections, Appendices A–K, and 25 result figures. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete material despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V3 reports original Monte Carlo experiments on finite-width neural networks in Section 6 and Appendix K, including kernel corrections, tensor convergence, and stability with depth.

after.justification: V4 retains these original Monte Carlo results in Section 6 and Appendix K, including sampled NNGP and NTK statistics and comparisons with analytical predictions.

M1.justification: The Feynman rules, tensor decomposition, recursion relations, and numerical procedures remain unchanged. V4 reproduces Appendix D's selection rules in Section 4.1 and illustrates existing construction steps without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic inputs and MLP experiments with GeLU, ReLU, LeakyReLU, and identity activations. Single-input and distinct-input cases, width convergence, and depth-dependent stability coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The same comparisons against infinite-width kernels and analytical finite-width predictions appear throughout. No comparison method is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices J–K retain the same input vectors, four-layer GeLU width study, ReLU depth study through 30 layers, initialization settings, numerical integration parameters, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The isolated correction tests, tensor convergence analyses, critical versus noncritical initialization tests, and activation-function comparisons are retained. Redistributing the appendix plots introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix J.2 retains the same ensemble estimation and uncertainty procedures. Corresponding figure captions preserve sample counts and repetition counts, including 100 repetitions for Figures 6–10.

E6.justification: All 25 result figures retain their plotted data and numerical caption content. Findings concerning agreement around width 20, stability at critical initialization, and absent diagonal corrections for scale-invariant activations are unchanged.

T1.justification: The theorems, recursion relations, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged. V4's intermediate diagrams and fixed-point explanation restate existing reasoning; the susceptibility relabeling in Appendix H leaves its defining formula unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about the all-order diagrammatic framework, NTK mean correction, gradient stability, diagonal exactness for scale-invariant activations, and multi-input numerical implementation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of convergence, criticality, and GeLU input scaling remain unchanged, as do Section 7's architecture and higher-order-analysis limitations. The new generic Impact Statement adds no substantive scientific qualification.

D1.justification: V4 adds an implementation repository link to the introduction; v3 supplies no such code-access link. The implementation descriptions, numerical parameters, hardware specifications, and runtime information in Appendices J–K are retained.

R1.justification: The same 43 cited works and research positioning are retained. Author–year citations and publication metadata updates, including the journal entry for Day and colleagues, do not introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: V4 adds short explanations of tensor roles and fixed-point stability, repeats selection rules in the main text, edits several passages, and adds an Impact Statement. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, extensively reflows mathematical displays, and adds intermediate construction diagrams in Equations (11)–(13). Appendix figures are substantially redistributed, often separating formerly paired figures onto individual pages; all original result figures remain.

improvement.justification: V4 makes Section 4.1 more self-contained through reproduced selection rules and intermediate diagrams, clarifies stability in Section 5.2, and adds an implementation link. These provide modest gains in accessibility and reproducibility information while retaining the scientific evidence, although some appendix plots now sit farther from their discussion.
